subject: English Comprehension
questionText:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

A decision has been taken to have the proposal reviewed by an external panel.

options.a: An external panel has reviewed the proposal.
options.b: The proposal is being reviewed by an external panel.
options.c: They have decided to get the proposal reviewed by an external panel.
options.d: The proposal was reviewed by the panel as per the decision.
options.A: An external panel has reviewed the proposal.
options.B: The proposal is being reviewed by an external panel.
options.C: They have decided to get the proposal reviewed by an external panel.
options.D: The proposal was reviewed by the panel as per the decision.

solution:
Explanation:
The given sentence is: “A decision has been taken to have the proposal reviewed by an external panel.”

Here, the main passive structure is “A decision has been taken”. The doer of this action is not mentioned, so an implied subject such as “They” is introduced while converting it into active voice.

Passive: A decision has been taken to have the proposal reviewed by an external panel.
Active: They have decided to get the proposal reviewed by an external panel.

In Option 3, “They have decided” is the active form of “A decision has been taken.” The phrase “to get the proposal reviewed” is a causative construction. It means that they arranged for the external panel to review the proposal. It does not make the entire sentence a passive-voice answer; the main verb “have decided” is active.

Also, “get + object + past participle” is a causative structure: get the proposal reviewed = arrange for someone to review the proposal.

Why the other options are incorrect:
• Option 1: Changes the meaning. It says the external panel has already reviewed the proposal.
• Option 2: “is being reviewed” is passive and also changes the tense.
• Option 4: “was reviewed” is passive and changes the tense/meaning.

Therefore, Option 3 is correct because it changes the main passive structure “A decision has been taken” into the active structure “They have decided”, while retaining the original meaning through the causative expression “get the proposal reviewed.”

Ans: They have decided to get the proposal reviewed by an external panel.

questionText:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The documents had been submitted by the assistant before the deadline.

options.a: The assistant submits the documents before the deadline.
options.b: The assistant had submitted the documents before the deadline.
options.c: The assistant was submitting the documents before the deadline.
options.d: The assistant is submitting the documents before the deadline.
options.A: The assistant submits the documents before the deadline.
options.B: The assistant had submitted the documents before the deadline.
options.C: The assistant was submitting the documents before the deadline.
options.D: The assistant is submitting the documents before the deadline.

solution:
Rule: The past perfect passive ('had been submitted') converts to the past perfect active ('had submitted'). The agent becomes the subject.
The passive sentence "The documents had been submitted by the assistant..." is in the past perfect tense. To convert to active, the agent 'the assistant' becomes the subject. The verb phrase 'had been submitted' changes to 'had submitted'.
Option 1 uses the simple present. Option 3 uses the past continuous. Option 4 uses the present continuous.
Correct Answer is The assistant had submitted the documents before the deadline because it correctly uses the active past perfect tense.
Ans: The assistant had submitted the documents before the deadline.

questionText:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The possibility of the files being leaked before the official release was not ruled out.

options.a: Officials ruled out the leak before the files were released.
options.b: The leak of the files was ruled out before the release.
options.c: Someone did not rule out the possibility that the files were leaked before release.
options.d: The release happened before ruling out the leak possibility.
options.A: Officials ruled out the leak before the files were released.
options.B: The leak of the files was ruled out before the release.
options.C: Someone did not rule out the possibility that the files were leaked before release.
options.D: The release happened before ruling out the leak possibility.

solution:
Rule: When converting from passive to active, identify the logical subject performing the action. The passive structure 'was not ruled out' becomes active 'did not rule out'.
The passive sentence "The possibility... was not ruled out" has an implied subject. To make it active, a logical subject like 'Someone' is introduced. The verb phrase 'was not ruled out' changes to 'did not rule out'.
Option 1 changes the meaning to a statement of fact. Option 2 remains in passive voice. Option 4 changes the order and meaning.
Correct Answer is Someone did not rule out the possibility that the files were leaked before release because it correctly introduces a logical subject and uses the active past tense.
Ans: Someone did not rule out the possibility that the files were leaked before release.

The findings were interpreted to have been misrepresented by the spokesperson in the official release.

options.c: The spokesperson is believed to have misrepresented the findings.

options.A: It is believed that the spokesperson misrepresented the findings.
options.B: The official release was said to have misrepresented the spokesperson.
options.C: The spokesperson is believed to have misrepresented the findings.
options.D: It was believed that the spokesperson had misinterpreted the release.

solution:
Rule: When converting from passive to active, identify the subject performing the action. The passive structure 'were interpreted to have been misrepresented' becomes active 'is believed to have misrepresented'.
The passive sentence "The findings were interpreted to have been misrepresented by the spokesperson..." has 'the spokesperson' as the doer. To make it active, 'the spokesperson' becomes the subject. The verb phrase becomes 'is believed to have misrepresented'.
Option 1 uses 'It is believed' and changes the structure. Option 2 changes the meaning and structure. Option 4 changes the verb to 'misinterpreted'.
Correct Answer is The spokesperson is believed to have misrepresented the findings because it correctly identifies the subject and uses the active perfect infinitive.
Ans: The spokesperson is believed to have misrepresented the findings.

questionText:
Change the following from active to passive:

They feed the animals twice a day.

options.a: The animals are fed twice a day.
options.b: The animals were fed twice a day.
options.c: The animals are being fed twice a day.
options.d: The animals have been fed twice a day.
options.A: The animals are fed twice a day.
options.B: The animals were fed twice a day.
options.C: The animals are being fed twice a day.
options.D: The animals have been fed twice a day.

solution:
Rule: The simple present active voice ('feed') converts to the simple present passive voice ('are fed').
The active sentence "They feed the animals..." is in the simple present tense. To convert to passive, the object 'the animals' becomes the subject. The verb 'feed' changes to 'are fed'.
Option 2 uses the simple past. Option 3 uses the present continuous. Option 4 uses the present perfect.
Correct Answer is The animals are fed twice a day because it correctly uses the simple present passive.
Ans: The animals are fed twice a day.

questionText:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

New protocols are expected to have been implemented by the end of the fiscal year.

options.a: Authorities implemented the protocols by the fiscal year-end.
options.b: The administration expects to implement protocols soon.
options.c: Authorities are expected to implement new protocols by fiscal year-end.
options.d: The protocols were implemented as expected.
options.A: Authorities implemented the protocols by the fiscal year-end.
options.B: The administration expects to implement protocols soon.
options.C: Authorities are expected to implement new protocols by fiscal year-end.
options.D: The protocols were implemented as expected.

solution:
Rule: When converting from passive to active, identify the subject performing the action. The passive structure 'are expected to have been implemented' becomes active 'are expected to implement'.
The passive sentence "New protocols are expected to have been implemented by the authorities..." has 'the authorities' as the doer. To make it active, 'Authorities' becomes the subject. The verb phrase becomes 'are expected to implement'.
Option 1 changes the meaning. Option 2 uses 'expects to implement', which is a different meaning. Option 4 is a passive structure.
Correct Answer is Authorities are expected to implement new protocols by fiscal year-end because it correctly identifies the subject and uses the active infinitive.
Ans: Authorities are expected to implement new protocols by fiscal year-end.

questionText: Change the following from active to passive: They had been making the staff report discrepancies silently.

options.a: The staff had been made to report discrepancies silently.
options.b: The staff were made to report discrepancies silently.
options.c: Discrepancies had been reported silently by the staff.
options.d: The staff had been made report discrepancies silently.
options.A: The staff had been made to report discrepancies silently.
options.B: The staff were made to report discrepancies silently.
options.C: Discrepancies had been reported silently by the staff.
options.D: The staff had been made report discrepancies silently.

solution:
Rule: The past perfect continuous active voice ('had been making') with a causative structure ('make + object + V1') converts to the passive voice as 'had been made to + V1'.
The active sentence "They had been making the staff report..." is in the past perfect continuous tense with a causative structure. To convert to passive, the object 'the staff' becomes the subject. The verb phrase 'had been making... report' changes to 'had been made to report'.
Option 2 uses 'were made' (simple past). Option 3 focuses on 'discrepancies', changing the meaning. Option 4 is grammatically incorrect as it omits 'to'.
Correct Answer is The staff had been made to report discrepancies silently because it correctly uses the past perfect passive causative structure.
Ans: The staff had been made to report discrepancies silently.

questionText: Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure: The funds were believed to have been misallocated by certain board members over several quarters.

options.a: Certain board members believed to misallocate the funds.
options.b: Certain board members are believed to have misallocated the funds.
options.c: It is believed that board members misallocate the funds.
options.d: People believed that certain board members had misallocated the funds over several quarters.
options.A: Certain board members believed to misallocate the funds.
options.B: Certain board members are believed to have misallocated the funds.
options.C: It is believed that board members misallocate the funds.
options.D: People believed that certain board members had misallocated the funds over several quarters.

solution:
Rule: When converting a passive sentence into an active sentence, the doer of the action becomes the subject of the active sentence.

In the given sentence, "The funds were believed to have been misallocated by certain board members over several quarters", the phrase "by certain board members" identifies the doer of the action. The passive structure "were believed to have been misallocated" can be converted into the active structure "People believed that certain board members had misallocated".

Therefore, the correct active sentence is: "People believed that certain board members had misallocated the funds over several quarters."

Option 1 is grammatically incomplete. Option 2 is still a passive construction because "are believed" is passive. Option 3 changes the tense and meaning of the original sentence. Option 4 correctly changes the sentence into an active structure while preserving the original meaning and time reference.

Ans: People believed that certain board members had misallocated the funds over several quarters.
